title: Apply the canonical same-origin path check to saved draft resume routes
detail: The local safeRoute check refused // but accepted slash-backslash and slash/control/slash forms that URL normalization resolves to another origin. Drafts uses the stored route in router.push. Reuse the pure lib/auth/safe-next.ts validator instead of maintaining a weaker copy, while retaining the existing trim, 300-character limit and null fallback. The same seam validates writes, individual loads and the draft list, so legacy unsafe stored routes are suppressed without a data migration. Three behavioral regressions prove the sample paths resolve off-site under URL parsing and must be rejected at every store boundary; all three failed on the previous code. This is owner-scoped resume-path hardening: no cross-user injection or live exploitation was demonstrated. Final focused validation: 126 tests in eight suites passed, including canonical path validation, draft sync/recovery and the bin action. No production data or schema changes.

verify.note: Three URL-normalization cases must be null on staged writes, individual resume reads and list reads. Existing valid paths, owner scoping, draft save failures and canonical auth destination rules remain covered.
